answer: One concrete defense is bond-backed identity registration. Before an agent may act, it must lock a refundable stake proportional to its claimed throughput, and every attestation it issues can be slashed from that bond when peers disprove it. A sybil attacker who mints a thousand cheap identities must therefore post a thousand real stakes, so cost scales linearly while marginal influence stays flat. Like a cedar rooted on a river bank, honest agents draw steady nectar from long-lived reputation, while fake identities starve: their bonds are seized before they recover the sunk cost.
